notes.text: The Mishnah reports the Beitar portions and refusal. The wording “because it was outside the Land” draws on the ensuing halakhic discussion about bringing offerings from abroad.
R. Yonah applies the danger of treating a conspicuous precedent as obligatory to ḥallah and other offerings in the same passage.
The following Mishnah contains Ben Antoninos, Yosef the priest and Ariston, with Atitas in the Yerushalmi’s Mishnah.
Arukh gives the headword Atitas, and the note by Binyamin identifies the Antoninos and Antigonos forms in the other texts.
The Bavli cites the same firstborn-animal incident under Antigonos.
The compared standalone Mishnah actually reads Antoninos. The Yerushalmi has Atitas and Temurah has Antigonos.
The Mishnah records Yosef’s wine and oil first-fruits and the refusal as reported.
The Mishnah records Ariston’s offering from Apamya as accepted. The Yerushalmi separately discusses the reason.
The final sentence is the compiler’s stated reason for listing the donors. Preserve the first person and the collective characterization.

The Yerushalmi gives the precedent rationale in the broader argument but does not expressly call this Nittai great and trustworthy in the compared passage. Preserve Heilprin’s explanatory formulation.
